trajectory.development: The bond-keeping practices at work while the regularity still holds: markets, celebrations, craft and generosity keep friendships alive across moving seas. The author's Story Vision (E4) states this condition and E2 records the practices as d2. No existing Book is read (E5), so this is a placement in a proposed Book.
trajectory.becomes_available: A lived baseline: what the communities do to stay close, before anything tests it.
trajectory.changes: Gives d1's later failure something to break and d2's later test something to measure against.
trajectory.quote: Families maintain friendships across changing seas.

trajectory.development: The one trusted regularity fails: an inhabited island does not return when expected (d1). The Story Vision states that every known island had eventually reappeared within its expected cycle, so this is a break in the pattern, not one more migration.
trajectory.becomes_available: Made possible by the recorded expectation of return in E4; the baseline of the first stage gives the absence weight.
trajectory.changes: The practices of the first stage now read as resting on an assumption, not only as habits.
trajectory.quote: This year, one inhabited island does not return when expected.

trajectory.development: The disappearance tests whether the practices can adapt, producing repeated action families of reaching out, keeping faith and repairing (d2 under d1's pressure, the link E6 records).
trajectory.becomes_available: Requires the disappearance of the second stage; enriched by the baseline of the first.
trajectory.changes: d2 turns from texture into an engine of its own: the bonds now generate action.
trajectory.quote: The disappearance tests whether those practices can adapt, producing repeated action families of reaching out, keeping faith and repairing.

trajectory.development: In-world attempts to explain, exploit, mourn or reverse the failure, and the competing interpretations the Story Vision records. These are the characters' inquiries, distinct from d3, which is the author's design question about how much the Series discloses by the end.
trajectory.becomes_available: Requires the failure of the second stage, which E1 names as what every attempt responds to.
trajectory.changes: The absence becomes a problem people act on, not only a grief they carry.
trajectory.quote: The one trusted regularity fails, and every attempt to explain, exploit, mourn or reverse that failure generates pressure, action and revelation.

trajectory.development: Partial answers reached in-world reopen what else communities assumed was stable (E1). Inferred: what is reopened may include the practices' own assumptions, so the test of the bonds widens beyond the missing island. E1 says 'what else communities assumed was stable', not practices or relationships specifically.
trajectory.becomes_available: Requires the attempts of the fourth stage, which produce the partial answers.
trajectory.changes: The bonds tested in the third stage may be tested again on new ground, so d2 renews alongside d1.
trajectory.quote: Renewable because each partial answer reopens what else communities assumed was stable.

trajectory.development: Proposed: a practice built on the expected return, such as a homecoming celebration timed by generations of expectation, is now held for an absence. The practice's inherited knowledge goes silent at the non-return, so what the communities knew and what they could not know become one discovery, and those who keep the practice must decide what it is for. The record does not state that such a practice exists; this assumes a celebration keyed to the expected cycle, not one that predicts the migrations' order.
trajectory.becomes_available: Draws on the recorded expectation of return (E4) and the recorded seasonal celebrations (E2, E4).
trajectory.changes: Gives the bonds a limit and a human face; whatever d3 finally discloses can be read against what the practice knew and where it failed.
trajectory.quote: Every inhabited island known to the communities has eventually reappeared within its expected migration cycle.

relations.reason: The recorded link makes d1's broken pattern the test d2's practices face; without the failure the practices are not tested.
relations.quote: tests whether bond-keeping practices can survive a broken pattern

relations.reason: The test of the practices cannot occur without the disappearance; E2 names the disappearance as what does the testing.
relations.quote: The disappearance tests whether those practices can adapt

relations.reason: The test can occur without a dramatised baseline, but showing the practices first makes their strain legible and felt.
relations.quote: Families maintain friendships across changing seas.

relations.reason: Partial answers come from the attempts to explain or reverse the failure; without attempts there are no partial answers to reopen anything.
relations.quote: Renewable because each partial answer reopens what else communities assumed was stable.

relations.reason: d3 is the author's choice of how much the Series discloses by the end; the characters' attempts proceed whatever that choice is. No item records a constraint between them.
relations.quote: How far should the migrations be explained by the end

relations.reason: A craft condition of the proposal, not a recorded dependence: the homecoming practice lands harder if celebrations are shown before the non-return. No cited item carries a planting obligation.
relations.quote: Traveling markets, seasonal celebrations, shared craftsmanship, and acts of generosity help people sustain relationships even when familiar places become distant.

relations.reason: Proposed: a practice that fails at the non-return is compatible with all three answers d3 names; the failure can mean a deeper order, a broken one, or one never fully knowable.
relations.quote: fully explicable, partially understood, or enduringly mysterious

alternative_paths.ordering: Explicability first: the author develops d3's disclosure stance early, letting the reader understand the migrations' nature or the shape of its limit before the bonds are tested (s4 and the author's disclosure lead; s1 and s3 follow). Disclosure timing is a separate choice from d3's end-state answer.
alternative_paths.effect: Easier: an intellectual frame and dramatic irony as characters pursue answers the reader holds. Harder: the loss risks reading as illustration of a known mechanism. The characters' in-world partial answers stay available, since disclosure to the reader does not consume them; the reader's suspense moves from why to whether and at what cost they learn.
alternative_paths.quote: each partial answer reopens what else communities assumed was stable

alternative_paths.ordering: Bonds first: s1, s2 and s3 precede the search for explanation, so the loss is felt through the practices before s4 and s5 develop.
alternative_paths.effect: Easier: grief and the practices' strain are felt; s6's homecoming for an absence gains force; d3 stays open longest. Harder: early Books need momentum without an explanatory thread. Emphasises emotional reading; keeps every d3 answer open.
alternative_paths.quote: Communities act through practices (traveling markets, celebrations, shared craft, generosity) to keep relationships alive.

alternative_paths.ordering: The prior clue reading: the practices encode the migrations' order (routes, festival timing, craft), so the final disclosure reads back into domestic texture.
alternative_paths.effect: Weakened: the Story Vision calls the migrations unpredictable, which cuts against practices that encode their order. Practices keyed to an expected return, as in s6, survive this objection; practices that predict positions do not.
alternative_paths.quote: Their migrations are unpredictable, but generations of communities have learned to live with them.

opportunities.text: Proposed: a homecoming practice held for an absence joins d1 and d2 in one image, where the tradition built to welcome an island home must decide what it is for, and the bonds' wisdom is shown to have a limit.
opportunities.quote: This year, one inhabited island does not return when expected.

opportunities.text: What the practices knew and could not know gives d3 a measure: whatever the Series discloses can be read against where inherited practice held and where it went silent, under any of the three answers.
opportunities.quote: fully explicable, partially understood, or enduringly mysterious

opportunities.text: Inferred: a partial answer may reopen an assumption the practices rest on (that islands come home), so the bonds become where the reopening is lived, renewing d2 alongside d1.
opportunities.quote: each partial answer reopens what else communities assumed was stable

reader_experience: Bonds first gives the reader the loss as a lived absence: they know the celebrations and markets, so the non-return reads as something missing from a home they have seen, and later explanation is weighed against what it costs. Explicability first gives the reader a frame and dramatic irony, with suspense in whether characters learn. In either order the earlier Books keep their own experience, the practices under strain, whether or not the Series fully explains the migrations.
open_decisions: Which of d3's answers the Series reaches: fully explicable, partially understood, or enduringly mysterious.
Whether a practice keyed to the expected return, such as a homecoming celebration, exists in the world.
When the author begins disclosing the migrations' nature to the reader, separate from the end-state answer.
Whether any practice predicts the migrations at all, given the Story Vision calls them unpredictable.
uncertainty: The Story Vision (E4) is an excerpt and is truncated; later text may change these readings.
No Working Book element cites any development and no Book is read (E5); every placement is in a proposed Book.
The question names twelve Books, but no existing Book is given, so no stage carries a book number.
How 'unpredictable' and 'expected migration cycle' coexist is not stated in the cited items.

criticism_assessments.reason: Each point holds against the evidence: the explicability-first effect now keeps in-world partial answers distinct from disclosure to the reader and does not map timing onto end states; s1-s6 is now thematic preparation; d3-s4 is now independent; the rival-readings opportunity is dropped; 'unpredictable' is weighed.

The record supports an expectation of return and seasonal celebrations, so a practice keyed to the return is a grounded proposal; the festival itself is not recorded. Adopted as proposed stage s6; it replaces the order-encoding clue reading, which 'unpredictable' weakens.

changes_from_prior: The earlier sixth stage (practices encoding the migrations' order) was removed, not refined; a new proposed sixth stage, a homecoming practice held for an absence, replaces it, following c2.
The d3 and first-attempts relation is now 'independent' with no dependence, since no item records a constraint (c1).
The first-to-sixth-stage relation is now thematic preparation, a craft condition, not a causal prerequisite (c1).
The explicability-first path was rewritten and the rival-readings opportunity dropped; the clue reading is kept only as a weakened alternative (c1).
